summary.headline: Sell practical automation as a service; validate before building another SaaS.
summary.best_opportunity: Productized lead-response and booking automation for UK home-service firms.
summary.why_now: GOV.UK estimates 5.7 million UK private-sector businesses at the start of 2025, 99.18% small; that is a large addressable base, not proof of demand for any specific offer. A narrow service can test willingness to pay quickly without substantial upfront build.

top_opportunities.name: Missed-enquiry recovery for home-service businesses
top_opportunities.description: Set up enquiry capture, fast SMS/email replies, qualification and booking handoff using existing tools; charge setup plus monthly support.
top_opportunities.why_now: Large small-business base (GOV.UK 2025 estimates) and a direct link between response speed and booked work make this straightforward to test. Demand signal remains to be validated with local buyers.
top_opportunities.buyer: Independent plumbers, electricians, roofers and other appointment-led trades.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£600 for demo, domain, messaging and no-code/API tools; exclude founder time.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks if sold directly before building custom software.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly monitoring, changes and usage administration; medium-high if value is demonstrated.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong: engineering skills support integrations; sell as a bounded service, not a generic AI promise.
risks: Crowded CRM/automation market; differentiation must be a trade-specific outcome.
Messaging consent, data protection and unreliable integrations require careful setup.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best near-term test: interview and pre-sell a fixed-scope pilot before coding.

top_opportunities.name: AI-assisted admin automation for small accountancy practices
top_opportunities.description: Automate one repetitive intake or document-chasing workflow with human review and auditable handoffs.
top_opportunities.why_now: UK business population is heavily small-business weighted (GOV.UK 2025); small practices are reachable B2B buyers, but no live evidence here establishes their current buying urgency.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small UK accountancy and bookkeeping practices.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£1,000 for secure prototype, APIs and basic sales materials.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 2–6 weeks after identifying a painful, low-risk workflow.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good technical fit; domain access and trust are the main gaps.
risks: Sensitive financial data and confidentiality raise security/compliance burden.
Established practice software may already cover the chosen workflow.
top_opportunities.verdict: Pursue only with a practice partner and a narrow human-reviewed use case.

top_opportunities.name: Website care and conversion package for local service firms
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-scope website refresh, enquiry tracking, hosting coordination and monthly updates for firms with dated or ineffective sites.
top_opportunities.why_now: The 2025 GOV.UK estimate counts 5.7 million private-sector UK businesses; local outbound allows immediate testing, though the estimate does not evidence unmet website demand.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local trades, clinics and independent professional services.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£500 using existing web stack and low-cost hosting/tools.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks with a clear audit and fixed-price offer.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly care, edits and reporting; modest unless tied to leads.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong for a web engineer; scope discipline essential.
risks: Price competition from agencies and DIY builders.
Clients may churn if measurable business results are unclear.
top_opportunities.verdict: Viable cash-flow service; sell measurable enquiry improvements, not redesign alone.

top_opportunities.name: Niche lead-generation site for one local high-value service
top_opportunities.description: Build a narrowly targeted local landing site, qualify enquiries and sell exclusive leads to vetted providers.
top_opportunities.why_now: Can be launched cheaply with one niche and location; no current search-volume or advertiser evidence was available in this run, so commercial potential is uncertain.
top_opportunities.buyer: One or more local service providers willing to pay for qualified enquiries.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£1,000 including domain, hosting and limited test spend.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Usually 1–3 months; faster only with a buyer committed in advance.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Per-lead or monthly exclusive territory arrangement.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong build fit; requires sales and ongoing acquisition work.
risks: SEO rankings and paid acquisition economics are uncertain.
Lead quality disputes and dependence on one buyer.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not build until a provider agrees to a paid lead test.

top_opportunities.name: Micro-SaaS for recurring compliance or operational reminders in a niche
top_opportunities.description: A simple workflow and evidence tracker for one underserved UK microbusiness segment, sold as low-cost monthly software.
top_opportunities.why_now: A very large small-business population exists per GOV.UK 2025, but this run found no reliable evidence of a specific unmet niche need; validate manually first.
top_opportunities.buyer: One narrowly defined regulated or repeat-process microbusiness segment.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300–£1,500 for MVP infrastructure, domain and customer discovery.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Subscription if retention and workflow value are proven.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High engineering fit, weaker immediate-cash fit.
risks: Building before finding a paying niche creates substantial wasted effort.
Incumbents, changing rules and support obligations can erode margins.
top_opportunities.verdict: Treat as a later product path after paid service work reveals repeated demand.

best_pick.name: Missed-enquiry recovery for home-service businesses
best_pick.why_it_wins: Fastest path to cash within the £2,000 constraint: sell a clearly scoped outcome using existing software, then turn repeated implementation into a product. Broad market sizing is context only, not validation.
validation_plan: Contact 15 local trades and ask how they capture and follow up enquiries; document current process and missed-lead frequency.
Offer a paid, fixed-scope two-week pilot to 3 qualified firms; proceed only if at least one commits and baseline/target outcomes are agreed.
best_pick.first_offer: £350 setup + £99/month for one channel, automated acknowledgement, qualification and booking handoff; pilot pricing is a test, not a verified market rate.
best_pick.mvp: One business, one enquiry source, consent-aware autoresponse, owner notification, simple lead log and manual fallback; no custom SaaS until repeatability is shown.
best_pick.do_today: Create a one-page demo and contact 10 local firms with a short discovery question; make no custom build before buyer conversations.
